mission: Stage 1 Closure Wave — define all ten locks rapidly to bone maturity (not perfected); continuously test against Ownership · Capital Formation · Market Design · Household Economics · Power; then one final whole-system gap audit.

os_crosscut_test.ownership: Who owns, controls, bears risk, receives surplus?
os_crosscut_test.capital_formation: How does current production become future productive assets?
os_crosscut_test.market_design: What rules make markets produce broad prosperity instead of extraction?
os_crosscut_test.household_economics: Does the household end better off in income, assets, time, security?
os_crosscut_test.power: Does this prevent economic concentration from reconcentrating political power?

locks.title: Revenue and tax system
locks.problem: Arkansas (and the republic) currently funds core public functions largely through taxes on ordinary labor income and homeownership — burdens that punish work and local rootedness while failing to capture external demand, resource rents, enterprise surplus, and public-created value.
locks.objective: Fund public goods through prosperity-linked and external-income engines so ordinary labor income and ordinary homes can eventually exit the compulsory tax base — without shifting the same burden onto working households through a single regressive swap.
locks.governing_principle: Retire taxes on ordinary work and homeownership only after replacement cash is earned and reserved; unmodeled returns are not replacement dollars; COUNTABLE ≠ illustrative.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Ten-engine Public Income model (Use, Impact, Depletion, Visitor, Luxury, Human-capital, Value Capture, Enterprise, Prosperity Fund, External Income) feeding dual State and Community Prosperity Revenue Ledgers, with Residual Wealth Contribution only as a last self-retiring shock absorber on substantial surplus wealth by beneficial ownership — never ordinary labor income. Tax Retirement / Prosperity Fund ring-fence.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: Feeds LOCK-06 (municipal/county finance), LOCK-02 (capital formation via Prosperity Fund), LOCK-10 (transition sequencing), HYP-131 architecture, External Income / EICR, food-hub pathway (high-potential, COUNTABLE $0).
unresolved_questions: Which engines can clear free-cash and incidence gates at Arkansas scale?
What residual wealth floor/rate closes remaining gaps after engines grow?
Constitutional path for dual abolition staging vs hard cores (URT, debt service)?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: Feeder-binding promotions only with audited free cash
Stage 4 revenue sensitivity and recession stress

os_check.ownership: Public/community claim on surplus from public contribution and external demand
os_check.power: Residual wealth targets surplus concentration; engines diversify revenue away from elite capture of single tax base

locks.title: Banking, credit, and capital formation
locks.problem: Credit creation, interest flows, and investment allocation often extract value from Arkansas communities to distant balance sheets; local production does not reliably compound into local productive assets.
locks.objective: Ensure Arkansas households, firms, and communities can obtain productive credit and that savings, pensions, public capital, and local equity reinvest into Arkansas capacity.
locks.governing_principle: Credit should serve real production and broad ownership — not speculative extraction. Capital formation is the conversion of current surplus into future local productive assets.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Community/regional banking and credit-union pathways; public and quasi-public capital vehicles (Prosperity Fund, local equity, pension/local-reinvestment rules); credit access for productive enterprise and housing; clear separation of deposit/payment utilities from speculative leverage; disclosure of where interest and returns flow geographically.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: Joins LOCK-01 (fund capitalization), LOCK-03 (housing credit), LOCK-04 (small-business formation), LOCK-05 (anti-extractive finance), Geographic Money Statements, HYP-132 retain/attract.
unresolved_questions: What legal forms can Arkansas use for public/community equity without federal banking conflicts?
How to redirect pension/institutional capital without breaching fiduciary duties?
What credit-access minimums belong in household prosperity measurement?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: Local loan/deposit ratios and interest-leakage maps

os_check.ownership: Who owns banks, funds, and claim on interest
os_check.market_design: Credit allocation rules as market infrastructure
os_check.household_economics: Affordable productive credit vs debt traps
os_check.power: Prevent finance from capturing policy via concentrated capital

locks.title: Housing, land, and property
locks.problem: Housing cost, land speculation, zoning barriers, and insecure tenure dominate household budgets and block ownership; property tax dependence locks local finance to a contested base.
locks.objective: Make secure, affordable housing and productive land access normal for Arkansas households while preventing speculative capture of land rents that communities create.
locks.governing_principle: Shelter and productive land access are household foundations; unearned land-value gains created by public investment and community growth should not be privately monopolized without public/community claim.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Ownership pathways (including community land trusts / limited-equity where appropriate); anti-speculation and vacant-land tools; zoning that expands supply without destroying community character; property-tax replacement path via Community Prosperity Revenue Ledger (LOCK-01/06); renter protections that do not destroy supply; land stewardship rewards for working farms.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: LOCK-01 residual/community ledgers, LOCK-02 mortgage/credit, LOCK-07 infrastructure location, LOCK-04 worker→owner ladder, family/childcare location, aging accessibility.
unresolved_questions: Arkansas constitutional constraints on land-value capture and assessment?
Rural vs metro housing strategies without one-size-fits-all?
How to protect working farms while stopping speculative farmland financialization?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: County AV/millage and incidence maps (partially bound)
Rent burden and ownership rate series

os_check.ownership: Homes, land, CLTs, absentee ownership rules
os_check.capital_formation: Home equity and land as household/community assets
os_check.market_design: Zoning and anti-speculation as market rules
os_check.household_economics: Housing cost is primary surplus destroyer

locks.title: Labor, ownership, and small-business formation
locks.problem: Wages alone do not create security; workers lack ownership stakes, portable benefits, scheduling power, and a clear ladder from employee → owner → local employer → local capital formation.
locks.objective: Build a pathway where Arkansas workers can earn, own, start, and grow productive enterprises that keep surplus local.
locks.governing_principle: Broad productive ownership beats wage-only dependence. Labor power includes bargaining, ownership, portability, and time — not just hourly pay.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Employee ownership / co-op / ESOP pathways; portable benefits architecture; small-business formation supports (credit from LOCK-02, procurement from LOCK-06); scheduling and apprenticeship joins to HYP-133 human capital; anti-noncompete and mobility rules that fit Arkansas law; public IP/shared returns where public investment creates private enterprise value.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: HYP-133 education, HYP-132 retain/attract, LOCK-02 credit, LOCK-05 competition (franchise/PE extraction), LOCK-01 workforce prosperity contribution (incidence-gated), childcare as workforce infrastructure.
unresolved_questions: Which ownership forms scale in rural Arkansas vs metros?
How to design portable benefits without federal conflict?
What first local pilot proves worker→owner ladder?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: Stage 4 automation displacement under HYP-134 quarantine rules

os_check.capital_formation: Retained earnings and local equity loops
os_check.market_design: Rules favoring broad ownership over extraction
os_check.power: Disperse workplace power; reduce dependence on single employers

locks.title: Corporate concentration and competition
locks.problem: Monopoly, consolidation, franchise extraction, private equity strip-mining, and absentee ownership drain local wealth and convert market power into political power.
locks.objective: Design markets so competition, public options, cooperatives, and ownership incentives produce broad prosperity rather than extraction.
locks.governing_principle: Not government versus markets — rules that make markets serve households and communities. Anti-monopoly is prosperity architecture.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Competition policy and merger scrutiny adapted to Arkansas sectors (food processing, retail, healthcare, finance); public-option or yardstick competition where natural monopoly or capture is chronic; franchise/PE disclosure and anti-extraction covenants for public benefits; procurement preference for competitive local suppliers (LOCK-06); ownership incentives that reward distributed capital.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: LOCK-04 small business, LOCK-01 external income capture, food-hub ownership pathway, energy public participation, LOCK-09 political-power controls, OS-MARKET-DESIGN.
unresolved_questions: State vs federal antitrust authority boundaries?
Which Arkansas sectors are most concentrated and most extractive?
When is a public option superior to regulation alone?

os_check.household_economics: Prices, wages, and quality of essential goods

locks.title: State/local government finance and procurement
locks.problem: Cities and counties depend heavily on property tax; public purchasing often leaks to out-of-state vendors; federalism (grants, preemption, transfers) is not designed for a prosperity-engine revenue model.
locks.objective: Give municipalities and counties a post-property-tax-viable finance model and turn public dollars into Arkansas supply-chain and firm capacity.
locks.governing_principle: Public money is community capital. Procurement and intergovernmental design must build local productive capacity while protecting hard cores (schools, debt, essential services).
locks.proposed_mechanism: Community Prosperity Revenue Ledger replacements millage-class by millage-class; procurement rules favoring Arkansas competitive firms without illegal preference traps; transparent grant/preemption matrix; shared services and regional authorities with accountability; AEDC incentive→equity conversion path (legal memo parallel).
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: LOCK-01 engines, LOCK-05 market rules, LOCK-07 infrastructure funding, LOCK-10 transition (no service collapse), federalism framework.
unresolved_questions: URT / school foundation hard-core path under replacement?
Legal design of Arkansas-first procurement within commerce clause?
County capacity variation — what must be regionalized?

os_check.household_economics: Local service quality and tax burden

locks.title: Transportation, water, digital, and core infrastructure
locks.problem: Mobility, water, and digital access determine whether households can work, learn, age in place, and whether communities can host productive enterprise; infrastructure can either build shared capacity or become extractive private monopoly.
locks.objective: Guarantee reliable mobility, water stewardship, and digital access as household and enterprise foundations with clear public claim where public assets enable private surplus.
locks.governing_principle: Core infrastructure is shared productive capacity. Water and watersheds are long-horizon resilience assets. Digital access is economic participation infrastructure.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Integrated infrastructure stack: roads/transit/rural mobility; watershed and water-rights stewardship; broadband / public-option digital layers where markets fail; cybersecurity baselines for public systems; pricing and ownership rules that prevent private monopoly rents on essential access; joins to energy sovereignty and food logistics.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: LOCK-03 housing location, LOCK-04 labor access, LOCK-01 use/depletion engines, LOCK-08 data/AI access, resilience five-state tests, rural revitalization.
unresolved_questions: Arkansas water-rights and agricultural use conflicts under climate stress?
Public vs private broadband ownership models by county type?
Mobility minimums for aging and disability participation?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: Water stress and agricultural use data

os_check.ownership: Who owns pipes, spectrum, roads, data centers
os_check.household_economics: Commute, water, internet costs and time

locks.title: Data rights, civil liberties, and AI governance
locks.problem: Integrated AI/state systems can enlarge prosperity or enable surveillance and data abuse; civil liberties must constrain re-engineered government; AI ownership and surplus claims are unresolved (HYP-134).
locks.objective: Enable productive use of data and AI for Arkansas prosperity while hard-limiting surveillance, discrimination, and concentrated control of digital power.
locks.governing_principle: Government may be redesigned to serve prosperity — never to erase constitutional rights. Dual claims on AI-enabled surplus without government ownership of AI. Privacy and due process are non-negotiable.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Data-minimization and purpose limits; citizen data rights; AI procurement and audit rules for public agencies; anti-surveillance firewalls; HYP-134 parallel evidence posture until series bound; public research/IP return proportional to public contribution; digital identity that enables services without creating a control state.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: LOCK-07 digital infrastructure, LOCK-09 administrative design, LOCK-04/01 public IP returns, HYP-134 quarantine from COUNTABLE revenue, democracy frameworks.
unresolved_questions: What Arkansas statutory floor exceeds federal privacy minima?
How to audit public AI systems without freezing beneficial uses?
When do AI productivity gains enter ownership comparisons (gated)?

os_check.ownership: Who owns data, models, and surplus claims
os_check.power: Critical — information power is political power

locks.title: Administrative government, anti-corruption, and political-power controls
locks.problem: Economic reform fails if concentrated wealth can buy the rules back; agencies, boards, and authorities can drift into capture; campaign finance and lobbying reconcentrate political power.
locks.objective: Design administrative and political rules so Constitutional Capitalism cannot be quietly reversed by the wealth it refuses to let dominate.
locks.governing_principle: Prevent economic concentration from reconcentrating political power. Accountability, transparency, sunset, and conflict-of-interest rules are system architecture — not afterthoughts.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Agency performance and sunset review; open contracting; lobbying/campaign-finance constraints aligned with free-speech doctrine but hostile to pay-to-play; revolving-door limits; forensic audit governance; civic participation channels already framed in democracy modules; beneficial-ownership transparency joining LOCK-01 residual wealth.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: OS-POWER (home lock), LOCK-05 competition, LOCK-06 procurement, LOCK-08 data rights, OpenFEC/OpenStates infrastructure already built, justice/public-safety first-pass structures.
unresolved_questions: What package survives Arkansas and federal constitutional review?
How to fund politics without donor capture or state monopoly of speech?
Which boards/authorities are highest capture risk?
later_evidence_testing_requirements: Stage 4 political-capture and corruption attack scenarios

os_check.ownership: Transparency of who owns influence channels
os_check.capital_formation: Block diversion of public capital via corruption
os_check.household_economics: Services not sold to highest bidder
os_check.power: Core lock — possibly the project's most important idea

locks.title: Transition architecture from the current system to the new one
locks.problem: Moving from today's tax, finance, service, and ownership arrangements can break pensions, credit, schools, and markets if sequencing is wrong; abolish-today impulses destroy credibility.
locks.objective: Sequence the shift so engines come online, hard cores stay funded, households gain security, and no critical service or obligation collapses during transition.
locks.governing_principle: No abolish-today. Earn retirement of old bases. Pilot locally, measure, expand. Resilience stress-test validates; it does not invent revenue.
locks.proposed_mechanism: Milestone chain: Evidence → Comparative Diagnosis → Arkansas Needs → Human Capability → Local Pilot → Retain/Attract → Public Income & Ownership → Resilience Stress Test → Legal Feasibility → Measurement → Expansion. Millage-class and engine-by-engine staging; debt/URT protected first; local proof principle; five-state resilience as Stage 4 validation framework; Stage 2 first-pass fills bones before Stage 3 vertical depth.
locks.relationship_to_other_modules: All locks; HYP-129 pilots; HYP-130 needs; HYP-131 engines; HYP-132–134 parallel tracks; completion ladder Stages 1–4.
unresolved_questions: What is the first Arkansas pilot bundle that proves multi-lock interaction?
Legal amendment sequence vs statutory-first path?
How to communicate transition without promising unearned tax cuts?

os_check.ownership: Sequencing of ownership transfers without shock
os_check.market_design: Phase rules in without market panic
os_check.household_economics: No cliff losses for ordinary households
os_check.power: Transition must not create emergency powers that stick

stage_1_closure_remaining.purpose: One final systems-level completeness check — not deep research — to ensure no entire organ is missing
